instruction: Adult FAW moth around my farm mean say every maize plant get the pest?
response: No. Adult moths show say FAW dey around, but you still need inspect maize whorls for fresh damage or frass to confirm current larval infestation. Source: FAO FAMEWS/FAW monitoring guidance.

instruction: Fall armyworm damage always mean say my maize yield go drop badly?
response: No be always. Maize fit compensate for some leaf damage, so scout current infestation and assess the field instead of assuming every damaged plant will lose most of its yield. Source: FAO FAW management guidance (2018).

instruction: I see old holes but no fresh frass. Wetin I suppose do?
response: No make treatment decision from old damage alone. Recheck the whorl for fresh damage or fresh frass and count only plants with current signs. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018).

instruction: Vision signal: 51% fall armyworm, 46% stem borer. Farmer: My maize dey damage inside. Wetin I do?
response: I need one more clue before I identify am. The fresh damage dey inside the whorl with moist frass, or you see holes and dry sawdust-like material along the stalk? Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: If my photo vision model says FAW is likely, should the assistant always agree?
response: No. When the vision score is close between FAW and another pest, the assistant should ask a targeted question about whorl damage, fresh frass or diagnostic larval markings before naming the pest. Source: FAO FAW Guidance Note 2 (2018); CABI Field Handbook.

instruction: Vision signal: 55% fall armyworm, 40% another caterpillar. Farmer: The caterpillar brown. Na FAW?
response: No guess from colour alone. Does the caterpillar have the pale upside-down Y on its head, and four dark spots near the last body segment? Source: CABI Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: The young leaves of my maize get pale scrape marks, no be holes yet. This one na fall armyworm?
response: Pale scrape marks for young leaves na sign of small fall armyworm larva wey dey feed before dem chew through. Check the whorl for tiny larva and fresh frass to confirm. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I fit know the difference between fall armyworm damage and stem borer damage?
response: Fall armyworm dey feed inside the whorl, e dey leave ragged holes and wet frass, but stem borer dey bore inside the stem, e dey leave borehole and 'dead heart'. Split some stems if you suspect boring. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: Something dey cut my small maize for the base for night. Na fall armyworm?
response: To cut seedling clean for the base for night na cutworm pass fall armyworm, wey dey feed inside the whorl. Look for larva for ground near the plant base instead of inside the whorl. Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Plenty caterpillar dey march across my farm and dey chop grass too. Na fall armyworm?
response: Plenty caterpillar wey dey march together and like grass fit be African armyworm pass fall armyworm, wey dey stay inside maize whorl with about one larva per whorl because dem dey chop each other. Describe the larva marks make e easy to confirm. Source: FAO/CABI FAW identification guidance.

instruction: Na only one caterpillar dey inside every whorl wey I open. This one mean say e no be fall armyworm?
response: No. Fall armyworm larva dey chop each other, so to see about one larva per whorl na wetin we dey expect, no be reason to rule am out. Confirm with the Y mark for head and the back spots. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How fall armyworm egg mass dey look and where I go see am?
response: Dem dey lay egg for cluster, plenty time for leaf, and e dey often covered with soft grey hair or scales. Check if the cluster get cover and where e dey for the plant. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: As I dey scout, I see small caterpillar wey don shrivel or get small white cocoon for body. I still need to spray?
response: Shrivel larva or parasitoid cocoon wey stick for body dey show say natural enemies dey active. Where dem dey, avoid unnecessary spray wey go kill dem, and rely on continued scouting. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: The maize dey tassel and dey form cob. How fall armyworm management take change?
response: Yes, for tasselling and cob time, check tassel, silk and cob join the whorl, because larva dey move go the reproductive parts. Weigh any spraying against the pre-harvest interval for the product label. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: The holes for my maize leaves look old and dry, no wet frass. Na active infestation be this?
response: Old dry holes without fresh frass usually mean past feeding, no be current infestation. Count only the plants wey get fresh damage or wet frass when you dey decide whether to act. Source: FAO, FAW Guidance Note 2 — Scouting (2018).

instruction: How I fit sure well well say na fall armyworm before I decide any action?
response: Join plenty sign together: feeding wey concentrate for the whorl with wet frass, the pale upside-down Y for the dark head, and four dark spots like square near the back. Any single sign alone weak pass. Source: CABI, Fall Armyworm Field Handbook.

instruction: How I go manage fall armyworm for the seedling stage of maize?
response: For seedling stage, the plants dey easy to damage, so scout well well and destroy egg mass and young larva by hand where e possible. Base any further action on scouting, no be calendar. Source: FAO, Integrated Management of FAW on Maize (2018).

instruction: My maize dey the whorl stage. Wetin be the priority for fall armyworm now?
